claims.statement: Re-drawing the verifier coin inside every bootstrap resample widens the CIs of the per-task cascade statistics ((a) eta - eta_B, (c) J_lambda difference per cell, (d) C_info - min cost per cell) relative to X1/X3's fixed draw.
claims.result: CI-width ratio re-drawn / fixed over the 24 noisy settings: (a) median 1.003, wider in 0.53 of 336 coin-dependent configs (0 coin-independent), (c) median 1.003, wider in 0.52 of 2505 coin-dependent configs (87 coin-independent), (d) median 1.001, wider in 0.52 of 9508 coin-dependent configs (1620 coin-independent). Rule (set after the quick run showed ratios near 1): PASS if every median > 1.02 with > 50% wider. Interpretation: a fixed draw puts one coin realization into each task's value, so resampling tasks already reproduces the coin variance to first order; the re-draw changes the point estimate (expected coin instead of one realization), not the width. X1's limitation 'CIs omit coin-flip variance' overstates the effect for per-task statistics.
